$comment: Assets owned by gems that expect a Rails asset pipeline, mapped into our esbuild build.
Read by esbuild.config.js and by test/assets/asset_mappings_test.rb, so neither side
has to know anything about the other. The only runtime link between Ruby and JS is the
`bundle info <gem> --path` call esbuild makes to locate each gem.
loadPaths mirrors what the gem pushes into `config.assets.paths`. It is asserted against
the real registration by the audit test, and it is what the esbuild resolver searches when
a gem's stylesheet references a sibling asset by logical path (Avo's webfonts do this).
Paths are relative to the gem root.
entries are the assets we actually emit. `target` is the output path without extension;
a `*` in it is replaced by the matched file's basename. Targets use the gem's own logical
names, the way Propshaft would resolve them — `avo/logo` for `image_tag "avo/logo.png"`.
precompiled_assets looks under `images/` first for typed helpers and falls back to the
undecorated name, so one entry per asset answers both typed and untyped lookups.
Known limitation: the audit only sees what a gem registers explicitly. Propshaft also adds
every engine's app/assets/* children implicitly; assets relying on that (Avo's empty
avo-overrides files) are not covered here. We ship our own avo-overrides instead.
